previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old woman with alcoholic cirrhosis was admitted for confusion, fatigue, and worsening back pain. She had poor oral intake and symptoms of a viral upper respiratory infection. Initial labs showed mild dehydration with a creatinine of 1.0, but no signs of hepatic encephalopathy, infection, or acute kidney injury. Her mental status improved with supportive care and hydration. Back pain was attributed to chronic musculoskeletal strain, managed with acetaminophen. Tramadol and trazodone were held during admission to avoid sedation. Labs normalized by discharge, and she was discharged home in stable condition with instructions to follow up with her primary care provider and continue her liver disease management.
